text:
Alex R: heads-up: we just saw a cluster-wide GPU provisioning stall in us-west-2; nodes spun up but stayed in 'draining' for >3m because the ephemeral snapshot cleaner wedged on a few hosts
Priya S: ugh, saw the alert. which cleaner? the background snapshot gc?
Alex R: yes — the new incremental snapshot path. it got into a loop trying to rewrite a partially-corrupted lsn and hit repeated EIO on /local-nvme0
Jamal: I'm pulling logs now. curious if it's related to the recent trimming patch we rolled yesterday
infra-bot: Incident detected: provisioning_delay_us-west-2 > 180s (affected pods: 42). Link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/1943219876
Maya L: attaching log snippet, pasted from one of the failing hosts:
```
[2026-03-17T09:14:02Z] snapshot-cleaner: rewrite /local-nvme0/snap-idx-128.tmp -> EIO
[2026-03-17T09:14:02Z] fsync failed: errno=5
[2026-03-17T09:14:03Z] retrying rewrite (attempt 3)
[2026-03-17T09:14:05Z] purge: blocked waiting for writeback, queue_depth=512
```
Alex R: queue_depth 512 is suspicious — that host should be at 64. maybe our per-instance iops cap didn't apply after kernel upgrade
Priya S: kernel upgrade? we didn't target that fleet. which kernel version?
Jamal: host shows 6.4.0-rc2; master image used a new base that slipped into the autoscaler AMI list. it changed the block layer defaults (nr_requests, max_sectors_kb)
Maya L: so default queue depth blew up, causing write amplification during snapshot compact, causing NVMe controller thermal throttling and then EIOs
ops-oncall: any immediate mitigations? we have ~20% of new GPUs stuck provisioning right now
Alex R: temporary mitigation: disable incremental snapshot rewrite on the autoscaler path and fall back to fast-merge (no rewrite) for affected hosts. I've pushed a canary flag to the controller: --snapshot-rewrite=off for us-west-2 autoscaler group
Priya S: can you also add a node taint so new pods avoid those hosts until we patch the AMI?
Jamal: doing taint now: kubectl taint nodes nodepool-usw2-ami-rc2 key=snapshot-wedge:NoSchedule
infra-bot: Command executed: taint applied to 8 nodes in nodepool-usw2-ami-rc2
Maya L: ops note: we should throttle the cleaner's concurrency and set explicit iops limits via blockdev or fio cgroups until AMI is rebuilt
Alex R: Agreed. action items: 1) rollback AMI to previous kernel or rebuild with block layer overrides (owner: Jamal) 2) keep snapshot-rewrite off for autoscaler (owner: Alex) 3) throttle cleaner concurrency and enforce queue_depth caps via udev rules (owner: Maya) 4) run a fs-stress pass on a canary host before untaint (owner: Priya)
Priya S: I'll run fs-stress + fio overnight and report back in the morning
Jamal: starting AMI rebuild now, will include explicit /sys/block/*/queue/nr_requests=128 and udev rule to set max_sectors_kb=512
ops-oncall: thanks. keeping this thread open. ping me once we have healthy canary and I'll un-taint the nodes
Maya L: note for postmortem: we need release gating so base-image bumps can't reach autoscaler pools without tag approval. this slipped through because the AMI was auto-promoted
Alex R: +1 on gating. also add monitoring for sudden changes to /sys/block/*/queue/nr_requests so we detect regressed queue_depths quickly
Priya S: quick note — storage team hit similar EIO signature in staging last month, but we didn't connect it to kernel defaults. adding that to the postmortem
infra-bot: Reminder: create incident doc? Use template: /templates/incident-storage.json
Alex R: created incident doc: https://infra.redwood/incidents/1943219876-doc (will fill details) :thumbsup:
Jamal: AMI rebuild succeeded on canary, ran fio workload, no EIOs after queue_depth cap and udev rule applied. rolling patch to remaining nodes (staged)
ops-oncall: un-tainting two nodes now to validate provisioning path
Priya S: provisioning passed on canary, ops confirmed pod scheduling resumed
Maya L: closing loop: schedule follow-up PR to add gating to pipeline and update runbook for snapshot cleaner concurrency
Alex R: thanks everyone. keeping this thread for the postmortem notes.
